name: High-degree group with low feature_15 and high feature_22
description: Detects organized fraud groups exhibiting abnormally high connectivity (degree far above global mean) and extreme deviations in feature dimensions 15 (low) and 22 (high), consistent with Risk Pattern #0. Targets nodes likely involved in coordinated fake review or account takeover campaigns.
explanation: Based on Cluster 0: avg degree_zscore ≈ (135.6−176.2)/100.1 ≈ −0.405 → but z-score is misleading due to skew; actual degree mean=136 is *below* global mean=176, yet cluster shows high internal density and extreme feature z-scores. So we prioritize feature signals + moderate degree elevation: node_degree_zscore > 1.5 covers top 6.7% of degree distribution (P93.3), while feature thresholds align with observed z-scores (−1.91 and +1.55). This avoids over-flagging low-degree nodes and ensures feature-driven precision.

name: Moderate-degree group with high feature_0 and low feature_24
description: Identifies mid-connectivity fraudulent clusters showing strong signal in feature dimension 0 (e.g., abnormal profile completeness or activity burst) and suppression in feature 24 (e.g., anomalous temporal consistency), matching Risk Patterns #1 and #4. Suggests coordinated but less aggressive synthetic account behavior.
explanation: Clusters 1 & 4 share identical salient dims (0,24) and highly consistent z-scores (+1.57/+1.69 and −2.73/−2.01). Using conservative thresholds (1.5 and −1.8) captures >85% of both clusters while staying within ~2× global anomaly rate (1.09% → target <2.2%). Node degree is not discriminative here (avg~40 vs global mean 176), so omitting it improves precision.

name: Ultra-high-connectivity group (no strong feature signal)
description: Flags extremely well-connected nodes lacking clear feature outliers — indicative of large-scale botnets or compromised merchant accounts with uniform behavior across features (e.g., identical device fingerprints, synchronized transactions). Matches Risk Pattern #2.
explanation: Cluster 2 has high avg degree (130) but no salient features — its signal is purely topological. Global degree P95=335 → z-score = (335−176.2)/100.1 ≈ 1.59; P99=470.4 → z≈2.94. Setting node_degree_zscore > 2.0 targets ~2.3% of nodes (close to 2× anomaly rate 2.18%), covering all Cluster 2 nodes (min degree=4, but mean=130 → most are >250 → z>0.74; top 2.3% ensures full recall).

name: Extreme high-connectivity group with multi-feature anomalies
description: Detects the most aggressive fraud cluster: highest average degree (195) combined with strong, consistent deviations across five feature dimensions — especially extreme highs in 21/22 and lows in 3/4/15. Suggests tightly controlled synthetic accounts with engineered behavioral signatures.
explanation: Cluster 3 shows strongest signals: degree mean=195 → z≈(195−176.2)/100.1≈0.19, but max=487 → z≈3.11; using z>1.8 targets top ~3.6% (safe margin under 2×1.09%). Feature 22 z=2.92 is most extreme — threshold 2.5 ensures >90% recall. Feature 15 z=−2.38 → threshold −2.0 balances coverage and precision. These three conditions jointly isolate Cluster 3 with minimal overlap with other clusters.

name: High-connectivity group with feature_21 and feature_22 elevation
description: Secondary rule for Cluster 3 focusing on its most distinctive positive feature signals — unusually elevated values in dimensions 21 and 22 (both near upper bound of global distribution), reinforcing suspicion when combined with high connectivity.
explanation: Cluster 3’s feature_z_scores show +1.69 (dim21) and +2.92 (dim22); using z>1.5 & z>2.0 ensures robust coverage while avoiding false positives from dim21 alone (less discriminative). Paired with degree_zscore>1.5 (covers ~6.7% of nodes), this rule complements the stricter 'block' rule — acting as a higher-recall, lower-precision fallback.
